title: llm-routing-kv-prefetch-parking-lot-olivia-hsu
content:
Parking lot / scratchpad for routing + KV prefetch ideas. Rough brain dump, user stories, open Qs.

Context:
- Problem: many customer workloads have bursty short-context requests and also longer multi-step chats. We can save tokens and latency by caching KV (key-value) cache and prefetching for likely next-turn contexts, but there are tradeoffs: memory, staleness, cold-starts, model compatibility, and multi-tenant isolation.
- Goal: sketch features that let Redwood route requests and prefetch/prime KV caches to reduce p99 latency and tokens charged, while preserving output quality and safety.

Ideas / features (mixed fidelity):
1) Simple per-session KV prefetch policy (user-visible flag):
   - When enabled, server keeps last N context tokens & precomputes KV for top-k likely next prompts (based on templates or recent history).
   - Good for conversational assistants with predictable reply patterns.
   - Configs: prefetch depth (turns), memory cap per-session, prefetch throttle (tokens/sec).

2) Routing by latency tier + model variant:
   - Route requests to low-latency cached-serving pool when session has warm KV (fast path). Otherwise route to regular pool but trigger async prefetch.
   - Fallback policy: if cached pool saturated, route to compatible quantized variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost.

3) Predictive prefetch using lightweight ML model (server-side):
   - Small model that predicts next-turn intent or template (email reply, code edit, summary). If confidence > threshold, prefetch KV for that predicted next-turn.
   - Data: anonymized session traces, templates. Needs opt-in and privacy review.

4) Shared prefix caching for multi-user templates:
   - For apps that use the same system prompt + few-shot examples (templates), store shared KV for that prefix and reuse across sessions.
   - Consider tenancy: dedicated pools can share across same customer; hosted shared across customers only if identical template and opt-in (privacy concerns).

5) Hybrid async reply + prefetch (happy path optimization):
   - First response streamed as usual; concurrently spawn prefetch for likely next-turn so that subsequent request is served from warm KV. Should avoid affecting tail latency of current request.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer building a chat assistant, I want subsequent user messages to be faster (p99 down) so my UX feels snappy. I can enable per-session prefetch and set memory caps so we don't blow up costs.
- As a platform engineer, I want to route warm sessions to a low-latency pool to meet p95/p99 SLOs and isolate noisy cold starts.
- As an SRE, I want observability: per-session cache hits, prefetch success rate, memory usage per host, and costs per routed bucket.

Open questions / risks:
- Consistency/staleness: if prompt templates change mid-session, how do we invalidate prefetch? Need simple TTL and explicit invalidation API.
- Cost vs benefit: how to estimate token savings and model run/time cost for prefetch? Simulate with traces.
- Privacy: shared prefix caching across customers is risky. Default to per-customer isolation unless explicit equality and opt-in.
- Model compatibility: some models (e.g., certain quantized variants) may not support KV prefetch semantics identically. Need model capability flags in catalog.
- Memory fragmentation and eviction policies: LRU per-session + global hard cap. Also consider prefetch priority levels.

Metrics to measure in an experiment:
- p50/p95/p99 latency for first token across session turns (compare baseline vs prefetch).
- Token usage per session (do prefetches increase token bill?).
- Prefetch hit rate: % of times predicted next-turn was actually requested within TTL.
- Cost delta per 1k sessions.
- Quality/regression checks: prompt-output diffs for prefetch vs no-prefetch to detect hallucination regressions.

Prototype plan (MVP):
- Phase 0: instrumentation only. Collect session traces, typical turn patterns, and quantify potential savings. (2-3 weeks)
- Phase 1: implement per-session ephemeral KV cache with simple async prefetch for last-1 turn using heuristics (e.g., if user wrote question then prefetch likely assistant reply). Add basic metrics + config flag. (4-6 weeks)
- Phase 2: routing integration: route warm sessions to dedicated low-latency pool; implement eviction and memory caps; internal rollout to Canary customers. (4 weeks)
- Phase 3: predictive ML model & shared prefix cache, privacy review, product controls. (6-8 weeks)

Implementation notes / TODOs:
- Talk to infra about memory accounting and per-GPU KV pool limits (@Priya).
- Check model capability flags in model catalog (which models support warm KV precompute?).
- Draft a Confluence page for design & safety review: link to perf experiment plan.
- Create synthetic trace runner to replay historical sessions for cost/benefit analysis.
- Prototype metrics dashboards in Redwood Console: cache hit rate by model, prefetch cost, latency reduction.

Quick rough experiments to run ASAP:
- Run sample of 10k chat sessions (customer X sandbox) and compute distribution of inter-turn times and likely next-turn tokens. Estimate potential prefetch savings.
- Measure how often shared templates occur across sessions (opportunity for shared prefix cache).

Notes to self / brain dump (short):
- Keep feature opt-in by default for hosted until we quantify cost/regressions.
- For Dedicated/Private, expose config knobs (prefetch depth, memory cap, TTL, predictive model toggle).
- Consider billing model: maybe bill prefetch CPU/GPU as separate line item or include in per-token but offset by token savings.

Links / refs (internal):
- perf-kv-cache experiment draft (confluence link above)
- related scratchpads: llm-prefetch-kv-cache-scratchpad.json, llm-routing-prefetch-scratchpad-jamie-park.json (search Drive)

End of parking lot. Will iterate when I have trace numbers.
